messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: In the Mounjaro prescribing information, SURPASS-1 (NCT03954834) was a 40-week trial.
The trial was in adults with type 2 diabetes.
The adults had blood sugar that was not adequately controlled with diet and exercise alone.
Patients received once-weekly Mounjaro 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg, or placebo.
After 40 weeks, 78% to 85% of adults taking Mounjaro achieved an HbA1c below 7%.
This is compared with 23% of adults taking a placebo.
The average HbA1c change was -1.8% with Mounjaro 5 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -1.7% with Mounjaro 10 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -1.7% with Mounjaro 15 mg.
The average HbA1c change was -0.1% with placebo.
Triplet: ["SURPASS-1 (NCT03954834)", "treatment group", "placebo"]

The relation 'treatment group' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject clinical trial included the specified treatment or intervention as part of its study groups.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has participant': The study or trial specified by the subject entity includes the group or treatment specified by the object entity as a participant.
B. 'tested in': The subject drug was evaluated in the clinical trial specified by the object entity.
C. 'has clinical trial result': The subject drug has demonstrated the clinical outcome or result specified by the object entity in trials.
D. 'has related treatment guide': The subject drug is associated with the medical treatment guide specified by the object entity.
E. 'used after': The subject drug is used following the treatment or condition specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
